overall_status: Nominal operation verified; adverse-case envelope incomplete
fault_review_conclusion: Retain the exact frozen 10 s nominal design as an engineering prototype. 21 of 24 configured ordinary scenarios pass; all four deliberate failure controls produce their expected consequences. Two moving-descent power-loss cases fail the belt service allowance, including a combined weak-spring/doubled-delay case that exceeds the raw catalog screen. A third weak-spring/doubled-delay case stops after the specified settling deadline. The original controller, brakes, acceptance thresholds, geometry and nominal trace remain unchanged. Fail-safe payload retention, fixture clearance and engineered impact compliance require a separate hardware design and qualification; this model does not establish emergency-safe operation.

scope: Engineering prototype: nominal operation and revised CAD are computationally verified, but three configured adverse cases remain failed. Power loss disables gripper torque and can allow the puck to contact its nest and the descending gripper; two such cases exceed the belt service screen, and a combined weak-spring/delayed-brake case misses the 0.5 s settling requirement. Fail-safe payload retention and engineered impact compliance require a separate hardware design and qualification. Contact friction, belt compliance/tension, supplier interfaces, fatigue, tolerances, electrical safety and physical accuracy require hardware qualification. Inspection animation is not a replacement for this solver.
